questions.question_text:
The resultant vector of $-\frac{2}{5}\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}$ is $\begin{pmatrix}3\\-4\end{pmatrix}$.
What are the values of $x$ and $y$?

options.why: Divided by $\frac{2}{5}$ instead of $-\frac{2}{5}$.
Multiplied the resultant components by $-\frac{2}{5}$ instead of dividing by it.
Found $x$ correctly but calculated $-4\div\left(-\frac{2}{5}\right)$ as $-10$ instead of $10$.
Uses a factor of negative one quarter rather than negative three quarters.
Multiplies both components by $-3$ but forgets to divide by $4$.
Keeps the signs unchanged and therefore does not apply the negative scalar.

questions.solution_text: Multiply each component by $-\frac34$: $-\frac34(-4)=3$ and $-\frac34(8)=-6$. Therefore $-\frac34\mathbf p=\begin{pmatrix}3\\-6\end{pmatrix}$.

questions.question_text:
Work out the values of $a$ and $b$.
$\binom{a}{-3}=3\binom{-1}{b}$

options.why: Replaces multiplication by $3$ with addition of $3$: $a=-1+3=2$ and $-3=b+3$, giving $b=-6$.
Replaces multiplication by $3$ with division by $3$: $a=-1\div3=-\frac{1}{3}$ and $-3=b\div3$, giving $b=-9$.
Uses $-3$ as the scalar instead of $3$: $a=(-3)(-1)=3$ and $-3=-3b$, giving $b=1$.

questions.solution_text: Multiply the right-hand vector: $3\binom{-1}{b}=\binom{-3}{3b}$. Equating components gives $a=-3$ and $-3=3b$, so $b=-1$.
